# Sourdough Focaccia

This one rewards patience more than skill. Most of the work is waiting, and the dough does the rest on its own.

Yield: one 9x13 pan, serves 8

## Ingredients

- 500g bread flour
- 375g water
- 100g active sourdough starter
- 10g salt
- olive oil, a generous amount, for the pan and the top
- flaky salt and rosemary for the top

## Method

Mix the flour, water and starter until no dry patches remain. Let it sit, covered, for 30 minutes.

Sprinkle the salt over the dough and fold it in. Over the next 4 hours, give the dough a fold every 30 minutes or so, then let it bulk ferment on the counter until it's roughly doubled, which usually takes another 3 to 4 hours depending on your kitchen.

Pour a generous pool of olive oil into the pan, tip the dough in, and stretch it gently to the edges. Cover and let it proof overnight in the fridge.

The next day, pull it out and let it come back to room temperature and puff up again, about 2 hours on the counter.

Dimple the whole surface firmly with oiled fingers, drizzle with more oil, and scatter flaky salt and rosemary over the top.

Cook time: 25 minutes at 450F, until deeply golden and the edges have pulled away from the pan.

Cool in the pan for at least 10 minutes before slicing, or the bottom goes soggy.

Notes: a sluggish starter means a sluggish rise, budget extra time on the front end rather than rushing the bake.
